items.text: In the 2025 Wealthtender Voice of the Client Study, the top 2-3 most important financial goals or needs respondents said they would seek a financial advisor's help with were retirement planning and income strategies (63%), investment management and portfolio growth (53%), tax planning and optimization (29%), and estate planning and wealth transfer (26%).
items.quote: What are your top 2-3 most important financial goals or needs that you would seek a financial advisor's help with?... Retirement planning and income strategies 63... Investment management and portfolio growth 53... Tax planning and optimization 29... Estate planning and wealth transfer 26

items.text: In the same Wealthtender study, the most valuable role respondents saw a financial advisor playing was 'Helping me plan for long-term goals (e.g., retirement, education)' at 49%, ahead of 'Providing expert investment advice' (34%), 'Helping me feel less financial stress/anxiety' (28.2%), and 'Optimizing my taxes and savings' (27.2%).
items.quote: What do you see as the most valuable role a financial advisor can play in your life?... Helping me plan for long-term goals (e.g., retirement, education) 49.00%... Providing expert investment advice 34.00%... Helping me feel less financial stress/anxiety 28.20%... Optimizing my taxes and savings 27.20%

items.text: The Wealthtender study found that nearly 90% of client reviews about financial advisors focus on relationship quality, planning advice, and emotional factors, while only 1 in 10 centers on investments or portfolio management.
items.quote: nearly 90% of client reviews written about financial advisors focus on relationship quality, planning advice, and emotional factors, while only 1 in 10 reviews centers on investments or portfolio management

items.text: In a Goldman Sachs Asset Management survey, the top three most important investment goals for Millennials (born early 1980s-mid-1990s) were to grow wealth over time, plan for comfortable or early retirement, and achieve financial independence.
items.quote: Millennials (born early 1980s-mid-1990s)... Grow wealth over time | Plan for comfortable or early retirement | Financial independence

items.text: Goldman Sachs Asset Management's retirement survey found that major life events such as having a child, buying a home, funding college, or managing a significant financial hardship are especially common among younger cohorts: 66% of Gen Z and 59% of Millennials reported experiencing at least one major life event in the prior 24 months.
items.quote: Of working respondents, 66% of Gen Z and 59% of Millennials experienced at least one major life event in the past 24 months.
items.scope: Gen Z and Millennial working respondents

items.text: Goldman Sachs Asset Management reported a generational divide in how competing financial priorities (credit card debt, paying down student loans, saving for college, caring for family members, time out of the workforce, financial hardship) affect retirement savings, with Generation X, Millennials, and Generation Z reporting significantly higher impact than Baby Boomers, and Millennials the most impacted.
items.quote: Younger generations, specifically Generation X, Millennials, and Generation Z, consistently report a significantly higher impact from these challenges compared to Baby Boomers. Millennials, for instance, are noted as being the most impacted.
items.scope: Generation X, Millennials, Generation Z vs. Baby Boomers

items.text: Cerulli found that younger investors typically are more comfortable directing their own investing through online brokerages, meaning financial advisors looking to connect with these prospective clients must be able to articulate benefits outside of the investing realm, such as financial planning, lending, and tax services.
items.quote: Younger investors typically are more comfortable directing their own investing through online brokerages (e.g., E*TRADE, Fidelity), meaning financial advisors looking to connect with these prospective clients must be able to articulate benefits outside of the investing realm, such as financial planning, lending, and tax services.

items.text: Fidelity's 2025 Investor Insights Study found that generation X, Y, and Z investors are reshaping the advisor-client relationship with a focus on holistic financial planning, life goal achievement, and non-traditional investment strategies, and that these wealthy next-generation households seek transparency in advisor compensation and broader life guidance beyond investment management.
items.quote: generation X, Y, and Z investors are reshaping the advisor-client relationship with a focus on holistic financial planning, life goal achievement, and non-traditional investment strategies... these high-net-worth households seek transparency in advisor compensation, broader life guidance beyond investment management
items.scope: wealthy next generation (Gen X, Y, Z) households

items.text: A UBS next generation study found that when choosing a wealth manager, experience and expertise sit at the top of the next generation's wish list (79%), while more than half (56%) want advisors who can build trusted relationships across generations, and 41% value the ability to fully understand the next generation's needs.
items.quote: experience and expertise sit at the top of the next generation's wish list (79%)... More than half (56%) want advisors who can build trusted relationships across generations... ability to fully understand the next generation's needs (41%)

items.text: A UBS next generation study found that two-thirds (67%) of next generation investors say a strong personal connection with their advisor is important, and that women place greater weight on personal fit and regular contact while men focus on competitive pricing and specialist expertise.
items.quote: Two-thirds (67%) say a strong personal connection with their advisor is important... Women place greater weight on personal fit and regular contact, while men focus on competitive pricing and specialist expertise.

items.text: A Bank of America Private Bank 2026 Study of Wealthy Americans found that among younger married investors planning is starting earlier: 32% of Gen Z and Millennials have a prenuptial agreement (with another 15% planning to), compared with 15% of Gen X and 4% of Boomers and Silents.
items.quote: Among younger married investors, planning is starting earlier: thirty two percent 32% of Gen Z and Millennials have a prenuptial agreement (with another fifteen percent 15% planning to), compared with fifteen percent 15% of Gen X and four percent 4% of Boomers and Silents.
items.scope: Gen Z and Millennials vs Gen X and Boomers/Silents
